Port's GameTaskDraw(float dt) (GameTaskState.cpp:86-94) instead forwards its own 'dt' PARAMETER directly to s_drawFuncs, and never resets any equivalent accumulator -- it uses 's_taskState.totalTime' elsewhere as a monotonic (never-reset) accumulator, which is a different quantity. Medium confidence -- the accumulate-since-last-draw-then-reset semantics could matter when update runs more often than draw (decoupled tick rates), but this needs a re-analyst pass on the GameDraw/GameUpdate call sites in Game.cpp to confirm whether the port's caller already supplies an equivalent accumulated value before concluding how to fix it.

_Z12GameTaskExitv.reason: Same +0x10000 tool address bug (report cites 0x00109e84 -> real GameTaskExit is at 0x00119e84, confirmed via GhidraMCP search_functions: 'GameTaskExit @ 00119e84' distinct from the PLT thunk at 001039ac). Direct decompile: 'if (!task_initialised) return; task_exit[old_routine](); task_initialised = 0; updated = 0;' -- the binary clears TWO separate flags on exit: task_initialised AND a distinct 'updated' flag. Port's GameTaskExit() (GameTaskState.cpp:97-102) only clears s_taskState.initialized (the task_initialised equivalent); it has no analogue of the binary's separate 'updated' flag at all. That flag is set to 1 in GameTaskUpdate only on the steady-state update path (real state, not the first-frame-init path) and gates GameTaskDraw's draw condition ('bM_State==old_routine && updated!=0'). Because the port's GameTaskState struct lacks this second flag, GameTaskDraw's gate (stateIdx==prevState && initialized) can pass on the SAME frame a new state's init() just ran (initialized is set true immediately after calling s_initFuncs, before any Update() call establishes 'updated') -- i.e. the port can draw one frame early, right after a state transition's init(), before the new state's first real Update() -- which the binary's separate 'updated' flag would prevent. Add an 'updated' bool to GameTaskState (default false), set it in GameTaskUpdate's steady-state branch, gate GameTaskDraw on it, and clear it in GameTaskExit alongside initialized.
